text: Case study: a social media analytics pipeline — where volume, not complexity, is the entire design problem.

A hundred million daily users at fifty engagement events each is around five billion events a day, roughly fifty-eight thousand a second on average — and a viral moment can spike that a hundredfold on a handful of posts.

A naive design shards by time bucket, and every write for today's one viral post piles onto one bucket. Sharding by hashed content_id spreads even a viral post's writes across every shard instead of one.

A trending leaderboard is read far more often than it's written. Compute it from the streaming aggregation every ten to fifteen seconds, and serve every read from that cache instead of recomputing it per request.

A like count that's a few seconds stale is invisible; a pipeline that goes down during a spike is not — this platform leans AP exactly as Lesson 19 predicts. Next up: presenting a system design in an interview.
